body:
---
Touches: gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md, gateway/src/agent_gateway/catalog.py, gateway/tests/test_catalog_go.py, gateway/tests/_catalog_world.py
Class: fix

---
## Deliverable
The `config` source of GW-CATALOG-GO refreshes `ok` again: either the console read (`GET https://opencode.ai/console/api/v2/config`) is answered 200 to the key the gateway holds, or the source's contract no longer depends on that read.

**Not queueable yet — one operator fact is missing (see §The fork).** The rest is verified and is the draft of the queue body once the fork is taken.

## What broke (verified live 2026-11-19T05:20Z)
- `GoCatalogStale{source="config"}` active since 2026-11-18T16:15:29Z. `gateway_go_catalog_last_outcome{source="config",outcome="fetch-failed"}` = 1 (the `ok` series went to 0 between 21:00Z and 24:00Z on 2026-11-17); `gateway_go_catalog_age_seconds{source="config"}` = 134162; `gateway_go_catalog_models{source="config"}` = 28; `gateway_go_catalog_refresh_total{source="config"}` on this pod: `ok` 1, `fetch-failed` 6. `GET /catalog/opencode` → `sources.config`: `fetched_at` 2026-11-17T15:45:01Z, `last_outcome` `fetch-failed`, `last_attempt_at` 2026-11-19T03:45:09Z.
- The gateway's log at every refresh since (2026-11-17 21:45 per the dig; 2026-11-18 03:45, 09:45, 15:45, 21:45 and 2026-11-19 03:45 read by this sitting): `catalog: config fetch answered 403 (config read) — keeping the last good snapshot`. `(config read)` is the console read; the catalog read (models.dev, no credential) comes first in the source and did not fail.
- **The dig's cause is corrected here.** The finding reads "the endpoint appears to require auth … where it was open before", from a bare probe answered 401. The read was never open: GW-CATALOG-GO says "The console request carries the Go key as a bearer, a `User-Agent` and a fresh `x-opencode-session`" and the page calls it a read "which any Go key can read". A bare 401 is what a request with no key gets; the gateway sends the key and gets **403** — the key is recognised and refused.
- **The key changed class three days ago.** FU-313 (archived 2026-11-16): the operator replaced the 30-day key with "a 1-year service-account key (permission `models: request` only)", rolled 2026-11-16T18:44Z, and probed with it: "`GET /console/api/v2/config` 200, `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` 200". The same key read the console 200 until at least 2026-11-17T15:45:01Z (27 h after the roll) and has been refused since 21:45Z. So for about a day the vendor answered the console config to a `models: request` key, and then stopped. Whether that is a permission now enforced on that endpoint, or the key itself revoked, is not readable from here: the gateway logs the status only, and no Go request has gone through the rail since the onset (`gateway_requests_total{rail="opencode"}` has no increase in the last 30 h; `gateway_credentials_rejected{rail="opencode"}` = 0 and `gateway_upstream_auth_rejected_total{rail="opencode"}` = 0 say nothing either way without traffic).
- It will not self-heal on a refresh: every 6 h the same key meets the same answer. Nothing admission reads is known wrong today — the frozen listing is the 28 models of 2026-11-17T15:45Z (`gateway_go_catalog_policy_models_missing` = 0) — but from now on a model models.dev adds, drops or re-prices does not reach admission, because one failed read ends the whole source's refresh ("the first that fails ends the refresh with its outcome").
- With the `docs` source frozen too (#3533, a different cause on a different read), **neither Go source has refreshed since 2026-11-17T15:45Z**.

## The fork (the one fact this issue waits on)
What does the gateway's key get to read?

- **(a) A key the console answers.** In the vendor console: is the service-account key still valid, and does a service-account key have a permission that covers `GET /console/api/v2/config`? If yes, the operator re-mints (or re-scopes) and rolls it — no gateway change, the alert clears on the next refresh, and this issue closes on that evidence. The key mint is operator-only.
- **(b) The source goes without the console read when the key is refused.** GW-CATALOG-GO changes: a 401/403 on the console read no longer ends the refresh; the listing is models.dev's catalog with no overlay, and the refusal is shown (an outcome or a field of its own, so the alert and the view do not call it a plain `ok`). For this account the overlay has been empty since 2026-10-20 ("`providers["opencode-go"].models` is `{}` for this account"), so today's listing would be the same. What is lost: a workspace `"disabled": true` or a cost/limit override would silently stop applying — which is why this is a ruling and not a row: it trades the vendor-client merge (⚖ 2026-10-20) for availability.
- **(c) The console read is dropped outright** (the dig's option): the source is models.dev only, the overlay rows of the page (§Which rows the merged listing holds, §An override's fields win, the console rows of §A failed read keeps the last good and §What a fetch sends) are deleted, and the catalog needs no Go key at all.

Intake's lean: **(a) first** — it is the cheapest and reverses nothing; if the vendor offers a service-account key no such permission, **(b)**, which keeps the overlay for any key that can read it.

## If (b) or (c): the shape of the work (draft, for the re-rule)
- One ride: GW-CATALOG-GO on `gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md` (the `config` bullet, §A failed read keeps the last good, §What a fetch sends, §No key, no fetch; the key never logged, §What /metrics says about the Go catalog), `gateway/src/agent_gateway/catalog.py`, `gateway/tests/test_catalog_go.py`, `gateway/tests/_catalog_world.py` (`classify_touches` → `machine-merge`, 2026-11-19).
- Existing rows the change meets (read as the rows lens reads them): "an upstream error on the console read keeps the last good" (`config-503` → `fetch-failed`) and "an unreachable console keeps the last good" (`config-down`) stay; "the key never reaches a log line" (`config-401-echo` → `fetch-failed`, `requests?` 2) is the row a refused-key rule contradicts under (b) and loses under (c); "no key, no config fetch" (`key` unset → `fetch-failed`, `requests?` 0) is the same question for a missing key and must be ruled with it.
- Under (b) the alert annotations in `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/prometheusrule.yaml` and `go-catalog.promtool-rules` / `.promtool-test` gain the new outcome.
- Unverified, verify during implementation: the 403's body (nobody recorded it — a fixture for a refused key is cut from a recorded answer, Goal #3300, never hand-written); whether the vendor answers 403 or 401 to an expired or revoked key.

## Out of scope
- The `docs` source's parse failure and its new read — #3533, waiting on its own ruling. The two are not one change: a different read, a different cause, a different fix.
- #3293 (listed is not alive) and the headroom read (#3118).
- Whether a refused catalog read should count in `gateway_credentials_rejected{rail="opencode"}` — it reads 0 through this whole episode; not ruled here.

Origin: deep-dig finding `dig-2026-11-19/dig-r1-20261119T033004Z/finding-2` (`GoCatalogStale{source="config"}`). Authored by island intake 2026-11-19. Island: gateway. Lineage: standalone — no open `task/goal` names the Go catalog's console read in its `## Acceptance` (#3300 records answers, #3305 derives tiers, #3118 reads the account's headroom).
